Terms of use Effective November 19, 2026 Covers commutescout.com, the MCP server and API, and the CommuteScout Drive apps. These terms are an agreement between you and the individual who runs CommuteScout (“we”, “us”). By using the website, the live map, the assistant, watch-area alerts, the MCP server, the REST API or the CommuteScout Drive apps (together, “the service”), you agree to them. If you do not agree, please do not use the service. The short version A summary for convenience. The numbered sections below are the terms. Information only. Road data can be late, incomplete or wrong. Check your state’s official 511 or DOT source before you go. Drive safely. Set your route before you move, keep your hands off the screen, and obey the law, signs and officials on the scene. It is free and provided as is. No warranty, and our liability is limited as far as the law allows. Play fair. No abuse, no getting around limits, no false reports. API keys belong to your account; keep them secret. Plugins and data belong to others. Plugins can be run by other people, and the road data comes from public agencies. California law applies. Questions or disputes: start with hello@commutescout.com . It shows public road data from state, local and federal sources (incidents, closures, chain controls, wildfires, cameras, signs and weather), adds routing, traffic, an AI assistant, watch-area alerts and community road reports, and offers the CommuteScout Drive navigation apps for iPhone and Android, an MCP server and a REST API. Coverage differs from state to state, and the map says where data is missing. CommuteScout is not affiliated with, endorsed by or operated by any government agency. Agency names are used only to say where data comes from. Parts of the service are early releases (for example, the iPhone app is a TestFlight beta and watch areas are an invite-only trial) and may change, break or stop. The service is free. A paid Pro plan is coming soon; if we offer one, its price and terms will be shown to you before you pay anything. 02 Driving safety # Your eyes belong on the road. Never let CommuteScout distract you from driving. If you are in danger, call 911. Set your route and settings before you start moving. Do not look at, type on or touch the screen while the vehicle is moving: rely on spoken directions and alerts, have a passenger handle the app, or pull over somewhere safe first. This includes posting road reports and asking the assistant. Use a phone mount where the law requires one, and follow your state’s laws on phone use while driving. Obey traffic laws, road signs, signals, closures and directions from police, fire and road crews. They always win over anything the service says, including a route that tells you to turn where you should not. Use your own judgment about every route. A suggested route can be closed, unsafe, seasonal, unpaved, flooded, or unsuitable for your vehicle. The service is not designed for trucks, oversize or hazardous loads, or emergency vehicles. Never rely on the service for evacuation, wildfire, flood or any other emergency decision. Follow official emergency instructions. 03 Information only: data, sources and accuracy # Road conditions, routes, drive times, speed limits, traffic, weather, camera images, alerts and assistant answers are estimates built from public feeds, third-party services and other users. They can be delayed, incomplete, out of date or wrong, and feeds can stop without warning. They are not a substitute for your state’s official 511 service or transportation department, which you should check before you travel. The data belongs to its sources. Agency data is published by the agencies listed on Data sources . Map data is © OpenStreetMap contributors. Routing and address search are by Stadia Maps, live traffic speeds by TomTom, and weather by the National Weather Service. Their own terms and licenses apply to their data. 04 Your account # You can use most of the service without an account. To create one you must be at least 13 years old; if you are under 18, you need a parent or guardian’s permission. You are responsible for what happens under your account and for keeping your sign-in secure. Tell us at hello@commutescout.com if you think someone else is using it. Watch areas are an invite-only trial. We can approve, limit or revoke access at any time. Areas are checked about every five minutes for incidents, closures, chain controls and fires, and delivery is best effort: an alert can be late, missed or wrong, so do not depend on one for your safety. You can delete your account at any time, as described in the privacy policy . 05 Acceptable use # You agree not to: break the law, or use the service to harass, stalk or harm anyone; post false, misleading, abusive or unlawful reports, or reports that reveal anyone’s personal information; get around rate limits, daily limits, access controls or bot checks, for example by spreading requests across many addresses or accounts; scrape, crawl or load the service at volumes that degrade it for others, or attack, probe or disrupt it; use the assistant for anything other than questions about roads, travel and conditions, or try to make it misbehave; resell access to the hosted service, or present its data as official or as your own; or use the service for safety-critical or emergency systems, such as dispatch, evacuation or vehicle control. 06 API, MCP server and API keys # Keys belong to your account. Keep them secret, never put one in a web page or app that others can read, and revoke any key that may have leaked. A key can read your saved places. You are responsible for requests made with your keys. Limits. Requests with a key count against your account’s daily allowance, shared by all of its keys (currently 2,000 a day on the free tier). Requests without a key are limited per network address. Current limits are listed on the developer pages . We can change limits at any time. Revocation. We can suspend or revoke a key, or block an address, that breaks these terms or puts the service at risk, with or without notice. Showing our data. If you show data from the service in your own product, credit CommuteScout and the original source, tell your users it can be wrong and to verify with official sources, and do not suggest that we or any agency endorse your product. AI assistants. If you connect the MCP server to an AI assistant, the assistant decides what to ask and how to describe the answers. We are not responsible for what it says, and its provider’s terms apply to it. No guarantee of availability. We can change, limit or stop the API, the MCP server or any tool at any time. 07 Road reports and other content you post # Only post reports about what you actually saw, and only when it is safe and legal (see driving safety ). Reports are public: they are shown on the map and in our public data files without your name or email, and they are sent to the plugins you have switched on that accept them, as the privacy policy describes. You keep any rights you have in what you post. You give us a worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to store, show, adapt, publish and share it, including with plugin operators and in our public data files, for as long as we need to run the service. You confirm that you have the right to post it. We can hide or remove any report, for example after other drivers vote that it is gone. 08 Plugins and third-party services # Plugins add alerts from sources other than public agencies, and many are run by people other than us. What a plugin shows is its operator’s, not ours. We list plugins and check that they follow the plugin format, but we do not control them, do not endorse them, and are not responsible for their content, availability or how they handle data. A plugin you add yourself by address is your choice and your risk. The service also relies on other companies, such as sign-in providers, app stores, map tile hosts and push notification services. Their terms apply to your use of them. 09 The CommuteScout Drive apps # We give you a personal, non-exclusive, revocable license to use the apps on devices you own or control, under these terms and the open-source license of their code. The terms of the store or test program you got an app from also apply. Voices The apps can download voices that run on your phone. Their speech is computer generated. Some voices are based on third-party models with their own licenses, which are included with each voice download. If a voice is based on the Supertonic model, it is licensed under the BigScience OpenRAIL-M license, and you agree not to use the voice or anything it generates for any use restricted in Attachment A of that license . Apple has no obligation to provide maintenance or support for the app. To the extent any warranty applies despite the disclaimers below, Apple has no warranty obligation for the app; if the app fails to meet a warranty you may notify Apple, and Apple may refund any purchase price (the app is free). Apple is not responsible for any claim about the app, including product liability, legal or regulatory compliance, consumer protection, privacy, or intellectual property infringement claims. You confirm that you are not in a country subject to a US government embargo and are not on any US government list of prohibited or restricted parties. Apple and its subsidiaries are third-party beneficiaries of these terms and may enforce them against you. 10 Open source and our name # The software is open source under the MIT license at github.com/nicglazkov/commutescout and github.com/nicglazkov/commutescout-app . That license governs the code. These terms govern the hosted service we run. You are welcome to run your own copy, but please do not use the CommuteScout name or logo in a way that suggests it is ours or that we endorse it. 11 Copyright complaints # If you believe something on the service infringes your copyright, email hello@commutescout.com with: your name, address, phone number and email, and your signature (a typed name is fine); the work you believe is infringed; where the material is on the service, precisely enough for us to find it; a statement that you believe in good faith that the use is not authorized by the owner, its agent or the law; and a statement, under penalty of perjury, that your notice is accurate and that you are the owner or authorized to act for the owner.
